constraint_prompts.purpose: the poem's own lines are verified and timed to this reel
constraint_prompts.prompt: Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it. We talk for years, travel through time — we grow old together, I believe. Maybe we could have it all. Before I go, I call on my mother — in tears, speaking of an abyss she Before I go, I call on my father — his calming demeanor summoned from the yonders. We walk for years, east toward the sunrises, retracing his footsteps — my tears falling in the wave shadows of the inner harbor. We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken. Someone borrowed, and someone blue — yet, broken. Yet, heard.
